note: Both sets make the same systematic error of attributing the R-57.5 row values (17,080; 14,880; 2,423; 459; 2,882; 19,802; 15,852; 2,870; 3,920 Btu/hr or kWh) to R-47.5, so each has about ten misbound values. Set B is better because it binds real properties (heating/cooling load, heating/cooling/total energy use) and keeps the eQuest vs BEoptE+ conditions, whereas Set A's attributes are placeholders such as 'value 1', 'energy value 2' or 'energy consumption (column 3, value 1)' that never identify the measured property, and it even drops the software condition in two claims. Set B does mislabel the four BEoptE+ Btu/hr load values as 'energy use' and includes one trivial R-value claim, but overall it yields more faithful, interpretable claims. Neither set captures the 2.08%/0.51% results or the R-57.5 comparison.
